params.message:
Trend headlines say what the trend shows, and plain-edit applies chosen ones

The trend writer used the post-title voice: a coined name, a colon shape and a
memorable contrast, which gave 'Gen Z Builds Identity From Streaming, Not Family'
over evidence about trips, hobbies and style. TREND_HEADLINE asks for one plain
sentence at the size of the evidence; the Studio keeps HEADLINE_VOICE for posts.
checkHeadline holds the form (5 to 12 words, 70 characters, no colon, dash or
question mark, no sociology words) and a failing headline joins the one rewrite.
plain-edit --apply --headlines writes chosen headlines while the trend still carries
the old one, kept for --undo, which now walks back one kept row at a time.
